title: New York's 11th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New York's 11th Congressional District will determine who represents Staten Island and parts of southern Brooklyn in the U.S. House. Incumbent Republican Nicole Malliotakis, first elected in 2020, is seeking a fourth term in a district that has trended conservative and is the only Republican-held congressional seat in New York City. Democrat Michael DeCillis, a former NYPD officer and 9/11 first responder, is the only active Democratic candidate on the primary ballot and is running on a platform focused on protecting democracy, lowering costs, and opposing Trump administration policies. The district's existing boundaries were upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court in early 2026 after a legal challenge sought to redraw the lines, preserving the current configuration for this election cycle.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the NY-11 general election were found as of June 2026. The race is rated as Likely Republican or Solid Republican by major nonpartisan forecasters.

candidates.name: Nicole Malliotakis
candidates.summary: Nicole Malliotakis is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 11th Congressional District, first elected in 2020 after defeating Democrat Max Rose. She previously served in the New York State Assembly from 2011 to 2021 and was the Republican nominee for mayor of New York City in 2017. Malliotakis, the only Republican representing New York City in Congress, sits on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

candidates.name: Michael DeCillis
candidates.summary: Michael DeCillis is a Democrat running for U.S. House in New York's 11th Congressional District. He is a fourth-generation Staten Islander with 35 years of public service experience as a paramedic, 9/11 first responder, retired NYPD police officer, civil litigation attorney, special education teacher, and former chief of staff in the New York State Assembly. DeCillis is the only active Democratic candidate on the primary ballot after his opponents suspended their campaigns, and his platform focuses on protecting democracy, lowering costs for working families, and opposing Trump administration and congressional Republican policies.

forecast.rationale: No public NY-11 general-election polls exist as of June 2026, so the forecast relies entirely on structural and contextual signals. Nicole Malliotakis is the three-term incumbent Republican in a district described as having trended conservative; it remains the only Republican-held U.S. House seat in New York City. The district's existing boundaries were upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court in early 2026, preserving the current configuration rather than shifting to a more Democratic-leaning map. Michael DeCillis is the sole active Democratic candidate and has a compelling personal story (former NYPD, 9/11 first responder, attorney), but no polling, fundraising data, or public evidence of a competitive race is available. Major nonpartisan forecasters rate the contest Likely Republican or Solid Republican. Without district-specific polling, the race falls at the lower end of the "likely Republican" band—reflecting a clear Republican structural advantage but tempered by the absence of direct voter data and the distinct possibility that a well-funded Democratic challenger could narrow the margin in a general election environment.
